examples.translation: the patient was groaning all night

glosses: to utter a groan/moan
перех. сказать, произнести что-либо со стоном

examples.text: ― Ты опять здесь! ― простонала она, не приподнимая головы. ― Какой черт!
― Зачем это? ― простонал Алексей Александрович. ― Всем же все уже понятно!
― Начинается! ― глянув на стакан, простонал поручик. Щеки его зацвели сплошным тонким румянцем.

glosses: провести какое-нибудь время в стонах

examples.text: Всю ночь проохала и простонала белугой, так что семья хоть беги вон, ― отвечал стоявший за стулом; потом, обратясь к женщине, ласково сказал: ― Чего бояться, дурочка?

glosses: издать, испустить стон

examples.text: Тяжело раненный капитан, простонав, упал на ковер.
В эту минуту умирающий очнулся и простонал, и она побежала к нему.
― А-а-а, ― простонал он и снова потерял сознание.

glosses: перен. издать звуки, похожие на стон

examples.text: Только фрегат напряженно движется и изредка простонет да хлопнет обессиленный парус или под кормой плеснет волна ― и опять все торжественно и прекрасно-тихо!
Но вот и час простонал глухой колокол на далекой соборной колокольне.
Простонали мои воротца в улицу, заплетающиеся за траву, несмазанные.

glosses: A low, mournful sound uttered in pain or grief.
A low, guttural sound uttered in frustration, disapproval, or ecstasy.
A low creaking sound from applied pressure or weight.
To make a groan.

examples.text: We groaned at his awful jokes.
The wooden table groaned under the weight of the banquet.

My Lord of Hereford here whom you call King, / Is a foule traitour to proud Herefords King, / And if you crowne him let me propheſie, / The bloud of Engliſh ſhall manure the ground, / And future ages groane for this foule act, [...]

Designed to accommodate 60,000 people per day in the 1960s, the main concourse, entrances and passageways around the station were by then positively groaning under the weight of more than 140,000 passengers every 24 hours.

glosses: To seemingly creak under the strain of being heavily laden.

examples.text: That night the table in the outer dining room was just groaning with good things.
Bookshelves groan under the bloated weight of tomes detailing Great Straight Marriages.

glosses: To strive after earnestly, as if with groans.

examples.text: Nothing but holy, pure, and clear, / Or that which groaneth to be so.

glosses: To cry out, as in sorrow or anguish.
To weep, lament persistently or bitterly.
To make a noise like mourning or crying.

examples.text: The wind wailed and the rain streamed down.

glosses: To lament; to bewail; to grieve over.

examples.text: to wail one's death
My lord, wise men ne'er sit and wail their woes

glosses: To perform with great liveliness and force.

examples.text: Another outstanding surfer from Hawaii - Fred Hemmings. Fred only stands up on alternate Wednesdays, but when he does, he really wails.
At Boston's Roseland, as "the Count's band was wailing," he grabbed Mamie, an avid dancer. The "band was screaming when she kicked off her shoes and got barefooted
The band was really wailing as we quickly made our dance moves in a most provocative manner.
We had a nondenominational wedding, with a bunch of great Sufi musicians really wailing, and my wildly enthusiastic mother in attendance.

glosses: A prolonged cry, usually high-pitched, especially as of grief or anguish.

examples.text: She let out a loud, doleful wail.

glosses: Any similar sound as of lamentation; a howl.

examples.text: The wail of snow-dark winter winds.
A bird's wail in the night.

glosses: A sound made by emergency vehicle sirens, contrasted with \"yelp\" which is higher-pitched and faster.
Synonym of wale (“to choose; to select”).

examples.text: Wailed wine and metes
